[Warm, conversational voice, measured delivery] Here is the whole journey from source material to a finished video. [pause for 0.25 seconds] You provide the material. [pause for 0.25 seconds] The agent works out what it means, proposes the visuals for your approval, then produces, checks, and delivers the MP4.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

First, the source material. [pause for 0.25 seconds] An essay or documentation needs a spoken script and new narration. [pause for 0.25 seconds] A podcast, interview, or discussion already supplies the voice and the order of the explanation.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

To start, clone the repository and install its dependencies with npm install. [pause for 0.25 seconds] Open an AI coding agent in the project folder, where it can read the repository instructions and skills.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

Give it the source material and explain who the video is for. [pause for 0.25 seconds] For example, ask it to explain this repository to a new developer, using the existing Animation SDK. [pause for 0.25 seconds] Ask for a plan first, including any paid narration, before producing the video.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

The next stage is understanding. [pause for 0.25 seconds] The agent reads the material, or transcribes the recording when needed. [pause for 0.25 seconds] It identifies the main ideas, how they connect, and what the viewer needs to understand at each step.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

The skills guide this work. [pause for 0.25 seconds] Generate video essay guides adaptation from written material, and generate essay audio handles new narration. [pause for 0.25 seconds] Animate recorded audio guides the existing recording workflow, preserving its spoken content and sequence.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

Now, planning and approval. [pause for 0.25 seconds] The agent turns the explanation into visual beats. [pause for 0.25 seconds] For each beat, it chooses a supported animation, specifies what stays visible, and identifies what changes as the narration develops.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

A process diagram explains a sequence, such as a request moving through review to delivery. [pause for 0.25 seconds] A comparison explains a distinction, such as generating a new voiceover or keeping an existing recording.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

When a draft moves from an author to a reviewer, a handoff can show the change in responsibility. [pause for 0.25 seconds] The agent selects these existing patterns from the SDK documentation.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

You review the proposed explanation, the visuals, and any paid calls. [pause for 0.25 seconds] This is the point to correct omissions or change the emphasis. [pause for 0.25 seconds] Production and paid narration begin after you approve the plan.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

The final stage is production and delivery. [pause for 0.25 seconds] For written material, the approved script becomes one continuous voiceover. [pause for 0.25 seconds] For an existing recording, the original audio remains the soundtrack. [pause for 0.25 seconds] Both routes then use the same visual pipeline.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

ElevenLabs provides the high-quality, natural-sounding narration for this video. [pause for 0.25 seconds] For new narration, configure your API key and voice identifier in the local environment file. [pause for 0.25 seconds] The repository preserves the exact request, the recording, and the returned word timings.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

Those timestamps connect speech to animation. [pause for 0.25 seconds] When the narrator reaches a planned cue, the corresponding label appears or the diagram moves. [pause for 0.25 seconds] The visuals follow the continuous soundtrack, without adding a separate pause at every scene boundary.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

The agent writes the video plan in TypeScript. [pause for 0.25 seconds] That plan declares scenes, labels, relationships, movements, and timing. [pause for 0.25 seconds] The Animation SDK computes the layout and the state of each frame, then draws the visuals as SVG. [pause for 0.25 seconds] A thin React composition connects that output and the audio to Remotion.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

The responsibilities stay separate in the repository. [pause for 0.25 seconds] Skills live under the agents directory. [pause for 0.25 seconds] The reusable rendering code lives in the essay SDK directory. [pause for 0.25 seconds] Each video has its own script, audio request, timing data, and scene plan.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

Remotion renders the React composition using web technologies, including HTML and SVG, into video frames. [pause for 0.25 seconds] Run npm run dev to preview it in Remotion Studio. [pause for 0.25 seconds] The render command selects the composition and writes the MP4 to the output folder.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

Before delivery, the agent runs the code checks and verifies the rendered output. [pause for 0.25 seconds] The tests check geometry, visibility, colors, and important before and after states. [pause for 0.25 seconds] The exported file is also checked for its audio and video streams, duration, and successful decoding.

[pause for 1.25 seconds]

The finished MP4 is delivered with its script and reproducible production code. [pause for 0.25 seconds] The source recording is preserved, so visual revisions can reuse the same audio. [pause for 0.75 seconds]
